text:
elaine: Heads up — we need to update SIEM export gating for GCP audit logs before next Friday. Current export includes user_email and resource_name fields that legal flagged as PII for EU tenants.
markus: Noted. Is this about long-term retention too or just the export pipeline? :thinking:
elaine: Both. Legal wants daily exports to be masked for EU tenants and retention cut from 2y -> 180d for those streams. We also need a just-in-time (JIT) unmask/unwrap flow for incidents.
ryan: For JIT, do we want KMS-encrypted field-level masking (unwrap on request) or proxy redaction on export? Tradeoffs: KMS keeps raw but gated; proxy redaction is simpler at export time.
tori: My vote -> KMS field-level wrap + RBAC + short TTL unwrap tokens. That keeps forensic fidelity. We should require a ticket + manager approval for unwrap.
elaine: Sounds right. Can we sketch the unwrap flow here? Minimal steps.
markus: Flow idea:
1) SOC opens incident ticket with tag `needs-unwrap` and justification.
2) Approver (sec-manager) approves in ticket system.
3) CI/CD job calls our audit-gateway to request unwrap token:
```
POST /audit-gateway/unlock
{ "ticket": "I-1234", "fields": ["user_email"], "duration": 28800 }
```
4) KMS unwrap service mints ephemeral key + records audit log + returns token.
5) SOC uses token to query SIEM export API, token auto-revokes at TTL.
ryan: Important: every unwrap must be logged to the immutable audit index and forwarded to SIEM with separate retention (5y) for compliance. That way legal can review access requests.
tori: Agree. Also add a threshold to require 2 approvers if query scope > 30 days or includes > 10k distinct users.
elaine: RBAC changes: we need a new role `siem_unwrap_requester` and `siem_unwrap_approver`. Who owns role assignments?
markus: Access should be limited to SOC + incident leads. I'll draft the IAM policy. Basic example:
```
role: siem_unwrap_requester
permissions: [audit-gateway:request-unlock]
scope: org:SOC
```
ryan: Also add a policy in the audit-gateway to enforce `justification` length and rate limits: max 5 unwraps per engineer per month.
elaine: For retention: update export pipeline to apply masking rules for tenant region. Proposal:
- EU tenants: export masked, retention 180d
- Global security logs copy (masked or tokenized): retention 1y
- Immutable audit of unwrap events: retention 5y
tori: How about the SIEM vendor contract? Do they allow tokenized fields or do we need to pre-redact before sending?
elaine: Vendor contract says they can hold encrypted blobs, but we need a contract addendum for holding plaintext when unmasked. I'll loop in legal.
sec-bot: Reminder: Any KMS unwrap RPC must include `ticket_id`, `approver`, and `requester_email`. Unwrap events auto-create an immutable audit entry. :warning:
markus: Implementation note — the audit-gateway should reject unwrap requests if the ticket is older than 30d or missing incident severity.
ryan: For vuln triage: if a CVE requires bulk log search, open an SR with `bulk-unmask` and require security director approval + SRE lead signoff.
elaine: Can someone file an RFC for the playbook (RBAC, API, KMS, SIEM contract updates, retention changes)? I can review.
tori: I'll start the RFC draft. Will include sequence diagrams and sample curl snippets.
elaine: Thanks — add checklist items for: legal addendum, IAM role assignment, metrics (unwrap count, average TTL), and runbook for revoke on compromised token.
ryan: One more: add automatic alerts if an individual unwraps > 3 distinct tenants in 7 days.
elaine: Good call. I'll capture that in RFC. Parking: who approves exceptions for emergency access? We need an on-call escalation path.
markus: Emergency -> sec-oncall + security director approval via PagerDuty + post-incident audit. We should require a follow-up RCA.
elaine: Great. RFC owners: @tori to author, @markus for IAM, @ryan for logging/alerting, @elaine to coordinate legal. I'll ping people when draft is ready. :thumbsup:
